Non-profit in Luxembourg, since February 2025

Real queer lives, made visible.

Blom is a small team of volunteers in Luxembourg. Every two years, we put real LGBTQIA+ lives in the spotlight. We also give awareness workshops when a company asks and work with European partners against the disinformation that targets our communities.

Our identity isn't what puts us at risk. Invisibility is.

Role models changed the course of my life. Not through big gestures, simply by living authentically.

Manon Pézot, co-founder, to woxx (translated)

It's the feeling of being alone, of not belonging, of having to choose between being yourself and building a career. Authentic, reachable role models are one of the strongest protective factors against that isolation.

We are a handful of volunteers with day jobs, so we do a few things and try to do them well. Donations and sponsors decide how much more we can take on.

Edition 2, Luxembourg

LGBTQIA+ & Allies Role Models

Role models are people, collectives and institutions who live authentically, lead in their field and make room for others. We celebrate them so that anyone wondering who they are or where they belong can find themselves in a real person.

Nominate someone Become a partner
NominationsOpen to self or peer nominations

NomineesNotified by the jury

The Luxembourg Role Models take place every two years. Dates for Edition 2 will be announced on our LinkedIn and Instagram.

Categories

Young Leader

LGBTQIA+ people under 30 who show early on that being fully yourself leads somewhere.

Authentic Professionals

Employees, founders and liberal professionals who are openly themselves at work.

Media & Culture

Journalists, artists and cultural workers who humanise LGBTQIA+ lives through their work.

Community Empowerment

People who uplift others through advocacy, mentoring and creating spaces.

Community Empowerment Ally

Non-LGBTQIA+ people who support us with action, beyond symbolic gestures.

Collective & Institutional

Networks, ERGs and organisations whose practices go beyond rainbow washing.

From Luxembourg to Prague

Blom is a member of the European Pride Business Network. Two of our winners, Loic Choquet and Gaby Schneider, were selected to represent the Grand Duchy at the 2nd European LGBTQIA+ & Allies Role Models Awards in Prague in May 2026, the first time Luxembourg took part, alongside national ceremonies in more than ten countries.

The European events often focus on politicians and large companies. Ours stays grassroots: a place that connects people from every walk of life.

Made together with CVRCLE Collective

The first edition was a collaboration between Blom and CVRCLE Collective, a young group of artists and creators in Luxembourg. They designed and hand-made the flower trophies and ran the social media campaign that introduced each nominee.

For CVRCLE Collective, role models carry stories that deserve to be seen, shared and kept.

PRISM

Fight against invisibility

Protecting Rights through Intersectional Solidarity & Media literacy

Disinformation about LGBTQIA+ people spreads fast, rides on algorithms and fuels hate and exclusion. PRISM gives young people, educators and civil society the tools to spot it, answer it and replace it with real stories.

Join PRISMSee the plan
Month 2 of 12 We are wrapping up the launch phase: community consultation and research. Media literacy workshops and storytelling start next, so this is a good moment to join.

Why now

  • Young people need media literacy and resilience against manipulation.
  • Queer lived experiences are being silenced online and offline.
  • There are almost no inclusive, community-led digital tools to counter disinformation.
  • Democratic resilience fades when projects end, so PRISM is built to last.

Who it's for

LGBTQIA+ young people aged 15 to 24, with particular attention to trans, non-binary, intersex, racialised and disabled youth, and to those living outside cities.

And the adults around them: parents and caregivers, teachers, youth workers, media professionals and policy makers. Young people should not have to face disinformation alone.

What we'll do

Listen first

Community-centred research

We start by asking the community what it needs, then turn research into tools people can use, co-designed with participants.

Critical media literacy

Digital resilience

Hands-on workshops on algorithms, fact-checking and prebunking, plus algorithmic detox and awareness of SLAPPs used to silence activists.

Narrative justice

Storytelling empowerment

Real stories, told by the people who live them, to replace the narratives used against us and to link LGBTQIA+ and women's rights.

Civic tech

Monitoring together

Trained volunteers document disinformation in an open, GDPR-compliant, multilingual dataset, so patterns become visible and can be challenged.

In Bologna, Gruppo Trans works across healthcare, employment, education, sport, arts and culture: a counselling helpdesk, mutual aid groups, legal support, TWork job counselling and QueerGym.

Their PRISM team: G Birindelli (project coordinator), Andrea Ruggeri (strategy and narrative campaigns), Christian Cristalli (disinformation analysis) and Andrea Donati (youth inclusion and communication).

Join PRISM

PRISM is run by volunteers who live the realities it talks about. Whatever your experience, what counts is commitment, even a few hours a month. Some roles may be paid. You can also simply spread the word, or tell us about a story or a piece of disinformation you've seen.

Practical tips, created for the Rainbow Career Day

How inclusive is this employer?

You decide what you share about your private life in an interview. What should matter is your skills. Recruitment is also your chance to see whether a company's inclusion is real. Weigh what you're comfortable showing against your own situation.

Three situations, three strategies
  • Strong position (in-demand degree or sector): test openly, for example by mentioning your partner or community work. A suddenly cold atmosphere is a red flag.
  • Vulnerable situation (urgent need, visa): be cautious and put your financial security first. You can come out later, once the probation period is over.
  • Trans or non-binary, with a visible identity: be transparent from the start. Better to discover transphobia before you're hired than after.
Before applying: research online
  • Is the job posting written in inclusive language? Does the non-discrimination clause mention sexual orientation, gender identity and gender expression?
  • Is the leadership diverse? Do employees show pronouns in signatures or on LinkedIn?
  • Has the company signed the Charte de la Diversité Lëtzebuerg? Check the list at chartediversite.lu.
  • Does it support local organisations or have an LGBTQIA+ employee network (ERG)?
In the interview: questions you can ask
  • How does the company concretely support its LGBTQIA+ employees?
  • Is there an internal LGBTQIA+ network? Who runs it, and does management take part or fund it?
  • What diversity training exists? Is it mandatory, and does management attend?
  • Can you give a recent example of an inclusive action here? A truly inclusive company always has one.
Benefits and policies to check
  • Same benefits for same-sex partners: health insurance, parental leave, events.
  • Chosen names and pronouns respected before any legal change.
  • Health cover for transition-related care and the specific needs of trans people.
  • Risk assessment for LGBTIQ+ staff sent to hostile countries (art. L.312-1 of the Labour Code).
  • An explicit policy against discrimination and harassment based on orientation, identity or expression.

About Blom, Luxembourg, February 2025

Why we exist

Blom grew from three queer people, each on their own path. Through community and volunteer work, we saw how many voices still go unheard, even in our own spaces.

We have seen what visibility and honest storytelling can do for a person and for a community. Across everything we do, we amplify real stories so people can experience other realities. That opens minds, deepens understanding and builds empathy.

Blom exists so that people asking who they are, or where they belong, can recognise themselves in real people living authentically.

The role models aren't ideological figures. They tell the stories of real people, to break unconscious biases like self-limitation and self-censorship.

Julie Mocquard, co-founder, to woxx (translated)

Ideas waiting for more hands

These projects are on hold until we have the time, people or funding to do them properly. If one speaks to you, write to us.

Adelphia

Peer support for people in transition or questioning: networks, workshops and, one day, micro-credits, so each person could transition at their own pace.

QueerPreneurship

A community incubator for LGBTQIA+ entrepreneurs: portraits and podcasts first, then mentoring for a small group of founders and a showcase with investors.
